channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan President Lays Foundation Stone for Guliston-Kulob and Kulob-Shamsiddin Shohin Roads
item.description: During a working trip to Khatlon region, Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon laid the foundation stone for the construction of the Guliston-Kulob road (32.2 km) and the Guliston-Vose road (14 km). These roads are of economic and social importance. The Guliston-Kulob road will be a four-lane highway with a 17-meter carriageway, including bridges and underpasses.

item.title: Tajikistan's Trade with Four Central Asian Countries Exceeds $1.6 Billion; Kazakhstan Remains Key Partner
item.description: Tajikistan's trade turnover with the four Central Asian countries has surpassed $1.6 billion. Kazakhstan continues to be Tajikistan's primary trading partner within the region. Further details on this economic cooperation are available.

item.title: Wireless Electric Vehicle Charging Achieves 98.51% Efficiency
item.description: Chinese and British researchers have developed a wireless charging system for electric vehicles with 98.51% efficiency. The 20 kW system, similar to smartphone wireless charging, uses magnetic fields for energy transfer, eliminating the need for cables. It's intended for future autonomous transport.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Launch Up to 150 Public Services via eGov GPT by Year-End
item.description: Kazakhstan aims to launch up to 150 public services through the eGov GPT platform by the end of the year. This initiative is part of the country's efforts to digitize government services and improve accessibility for citizens.

item.title: Almaty to Begin Heating Season Early Due to Sharp Cold Snap
item.description: Almaty will commence its heating season earlier than scheduled due to a sudden drop in temperature. The decision aims to ensure residents remain warm amidst the unseasonably cold weather. Further details on the exact start date and implications for utility services are expected.

item.title: Expert Urges Kazakhstan to Retain 12-Year School Education System
item.description: Political scientist Gaziz Abishev advises Kazakhstan against abandoning the 12-year school education format. He argues that an extra year helps students make more informed decisions about their future, as 16-17 year olds may be emotionally immature. He notes that 18-year-old graduates often excel in international olympiads and university admissions.

item.title: Oil Prices Surge Over 50% in One Year, Impacting Global Markets
item.description: Global oil prices have seen a significant increase, with Brent crude reaching $100.69 per barrel, a 0.36% rise. Over the past year, oil prices have climbed more than 50%. While stock markets like S&P 500 and Nasdaq have seen modest gains, Chinese and Kazakh stock exchanges show mixed results. Cryptocurrency markets have also experienced a decline.

item.title: Almaty to Begin Supplying Heating to Residential Buildings on October 10
item.description: Due to a sharp cold snap, Almaty will start supplying heating to residential buildings on October 10, and to social facilities on October 9. The city administration announced the early start to the heating season. After heat is supplied, residents and building management will need to regulate internal systems to ensure even heating in apartments.

item.title: Namangan Officials Accused of Embezzling 1.3 Billion Soums in Preschool Subsidies
item.description: An investigation in Namangan region's Uchqo'rg'on district has uncovered the embezzlement of 1.3 billion soums in subsidies allocated to preschools that were not operational. Officials allegedly colluded to register non-existent educational institutions and divert the funds. Criminal cases have been initiated for embezzlement and abuse of power.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Launch Robotics Production to Boost AI Integration
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to commence robotics production with the launch of the Qazbot complex, aiming to facilitate the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov emphasized the need to scale digital solutions across the industry and integrate key production data into a unified Data Lake. This initiative seeks to enhance productivity and competitiveness.

item.title: Oman Proposes New Maritime Access Route for Kazakhstan
item.description: Oman has presented Kazakhstan with a proposal for a new maritime access route. This initiative aims to provide Kazakhstan with enhanced connectivity to international shipping lanes and trade networks. Further details regarding the specifics of the proposed route and its potential implications for regional trade were not immediately available.

item.title: National Statistics Bureau to gain access to tax secrets
item.description: Kazakhstan's Bureau of National Statistics will receive automatic access to tax secrets and confidential information through the Smart Data Finance system. This will enable quarterly data on taxes paid, social contributions, and foreign trade, as well as monthly data on exports and imports within the EAEU. Annual data on corporate income and environmental impact will also be provided.

item.title: UN Official Warns Against Abandoning Afghanistan, Cites Crises
item.description: Alexander De Croo, head of the UN Development Programme, urges the international community not to turn its back on Afghanistan. He warns of serious consequences over the next decade due to economic, climate, and humanitarian crises, exacerbated by a 20% economic contraction and the return of nearly five million migrants. Continued engagement is crucial for stability and human rights.

item.title: UNICEF: El Niño may affect over 347 million children in 100 countries
item.description: UNICEF warns that the severe El Niño phenomenon between October and December could impact over 347 million children in nearly 100 countries. Children may face extreme weather conditions, increasing risks of floods and droughts, leading to displacement, malnutrition, water scarcity, and disease outbreaks. Globally, 1.1 billion children already face multiple climate threats.

item.title: Oman Sultan expresses interest in reviving air travel with Kazakhstan
item.description: Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tarik expressed gratitude for Kazakhstan's hospitality and successful talks, noting the growing cooperation between the two nations. He highlighted significant potential for investment partnerships in sectors like energy, mining, agriculture, logistics, and technology. The Sultan emphasized reviving air travel and leveraging strategic locations for trade.

item.title: Sultan of Oman Invites President Tokayev for a Visit
item.description: The Sultan of Oman has extended an invitation to President Tokayev to visit the country. This invitation highlights the ongoing diplomatic engagement between Kazakhstan and Oman.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Oman a Proven and Reliable Partner in the Arab World
item.description: President Tokayev stated that Kazakhstan views Oman as a time-tested and reliable partner in the Arab world. He noted the upcoming 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations and highlighted a recent productive visit by an Omani delegation to Astana, signaling a new phase of cooperation.

item.title: First Visit to Central Asia by Sultan: What Did Tokayev Discuss with the Sultan of Oman?
item.description: The Sultan of Oman made his first visit to Central Asia as Sultan. The discussions between President Tokayev and the Sultan of Oman focused on bilateral relations and potential areas of cooperation.

item.title: Kazakh President and Sultan of Oman Discuss Joint Projects
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Sultan of Oman Haitham bin Tariq Al Said held expanded negotiations. Tokayev noted Oman's role as a reliable partner in the Arab world and expressed confidence that agreements on energy, transport, agriculture, and IT will benefit both nations.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Oman to Develop Trade Corridor via Omani Ports
item.description: Kazakhstan and Oman intend to develop a trade corridor through Omani ports and strengthen air travel. President Tokayev and Sultan Al Said discussed cooperation in energy, transport, agriculture, and IT. Agreements will be signed, including on joint projects like the Dunga oil field.

item.title: Russian Deputy PM Discusses Expanding Economic Ties with Afghanistan
item.description: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Overchuk met with Muttaqi to discuss expanding economic cooperation with Afghanistan. Overchuk stated that conditions are now suitable for launching practical cooperation between the two countries.

item.title: Soldier Survives Caspian Tragedy, Returns Home After Service
item.description: Conscript Nikita Udlov, who survived a tragedy during military exercises in the Caspian Sea, has returned home after completing his service. The incident occurred on September 24 when a storm swept a group of servicemen into the sea. Criminal proceedings were initiated, leading to the detention of five high-ranking Ministry of Defense officials.

item.title: Kazakhstan considers using AI to verify social media users' ages
item.description: Kazakhstan is proposing to use artificial intelligence to verify the ages of social media users, particularly those under 16. The government has drafted legislative changes to regulate online platform registrations for minors. The Ministry of Culture and AI would develop age verification procedures if the bill passes.

item.title: US moves bombers from UK base amid Iran threat reports
item.description: The US has moved approximately a dozen B-1 bombers from a UK military base following intelligence reports suggesting Iran may be planning attacks using drones. The Wall Street Journal reported that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was suspected of planning an assault on the Fairford base. US officials confirmed the relocation as a precautionary measure.

item.title: Tajikistan Begins Importing Iranian Oil, Raising Concerns Over US Sanctions
item.description: Tajikistan has started importing oil and petroleum products from Iran, seeking new energy sources beyond Russia. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources confirmed the imports began in late August. This move raises concerns about potential secondary sanctions from the US, which is aiming to cut Iran's oil revenue.

item.title: Textile Complex with 640 Jobs to Be Built in Kulob SEZ, Tajikistan
item.description: A textile complex creating 640 jobs will be constructed in Tajikistan's Kulob Free Economic Zone. The project, involving foreign investment, will include spinning and cotton-cleaning facilities, aiming to boost industrialization and exports.

item.title: New Head Appointed for Karaganda Region Emergency Situations Department
item.description: Manarbek Shapagatov has been appointed the new head of the Emergency Situations Department for the Karaganda region. The Ministry of Emergency Situations of the Republic of Kazakhstan announced the appointment, noting Shapagatov's extensive service experience.

item.title: UNDP Head Calls Exclusion of Girls from Education in Afghanistan Unacceptable
item.description: Alexander De Croo, head of the UN Development Programme, stated that excluding girls over 12 from education in Afghanistan is unacceptable and detrimental to development. He emphasized the need for the entire population's capacity to address challenges and highlighted UNDP's work supporting women's entrepreneurship. De Croo noted daily discussions with the Taliban regarding women's and girls' rights.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Move Services for Issuing IIN to Foreigners Online
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to transition the service for issuing Individual Identification Numbers (IIN) to foreigners to an online format. Additionally, 12 other government services will become exclusively online. This move is part of a broader initiative to digitize public services, aiming to streamline processes and reduce citizen interaction with traditional service centers.

item.title: Russia Accuses Ukraine of Deliberately Attacking Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Plant
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova accused Ukraine of deliberately attacking the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, aiming to cause a nuclear disaster. She claimed an attack targeted an administrative building near a reactor, posing a risk of a serious nuclear incident.

item.title: Kongratbay Sharipov Appointed Rector of Tashkent State University of Economics
item.description: Kongratbay Sharipov has been appointed the new Rector of the Tashkent State University of Economics. Prior to this appointment, he served as the Minister of Higher Education, Science, and Innovations of Uzbekistan since February 2, 2024. Sharipov has previous experience as the rector of this university and has held other significant positions in the education sector.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Man and Woman Sentenced in Case of 13-Year-Old Girl's Rape
item.description: In northern Kazakhstan, a court sentenced a man to life imprisonment and his partner to 20 years for the sexual assault of a 13-year-old girl. The man was convicted of violent sexual acts against a minor, while the woman was found guilty of aiding the crime. The court ordered compensation and banned the convicted from working with minors.

item.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan Activate Collective Defense Commitments
item.description: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have agreed to immediately implement their collective defense commitments, including rapid military force deployment to Saudi Arabia. The decision follows an emergency meeting of the Mecca Defense Alliance in Riyadh. The move reaffirms solidarity in responding to attacks against Saudi Arabia and Islamic holy sites.

item.title: US Central Command Reports 13 Ships Destroyed in Maritime Blockade of Iran
item.description: The U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced that 13 commercial vessels were destroyed over three months as part of a maritime blockade of Iran, implemented on July 14. CENTCOM claims these vessels were part of a network linked to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

item.title: Dushanbe Installs AI-Powered Traffic Lights Adapting Signal Times
item.description: Dushanbe has deployed AI-powered traffic lights at two intersections that analyze traffic flow in real-time to adjust green signal duration. The Ministry of Transport of Tajikistan reports the system counts vehicles, measures speed, and detects pedestrians to optimize traffic. This aims to reduce congestion.

item.title: Tashkent Officials Pledge to Consider Suggestions on Bus Fare Payment
item.description: Tashkent authorities will consider passenger feedback regarding difficulties in paying bus fares due to crowded conditions. Suggestions for ensuring validator functionality and convenient payment are being reviewed. The transport department aims to improve payment culture and compliance with upfront fare payment rules.

item.title: Human Rights Group Welcomes ICC Arrest Warrants for Taliban Ministers
item.description: The human rights organization Rawadari has welcomed arrest warrants issued by the International Criminal Court for two Taliban ministers. Rawadari stated the warrants are for alleged gender persecution and harassment of those opposing Taliban policies. The group urged governments to support international judicial processes to ensure accountability and justice for victims of human rights violations in Afghanistan.

item.title: Tajikistan Parliament Council Discusses Draft Laws and International Agreements
item.description: The Council of the Majlisi Namoyandagon of Tajikistan held a session discussing draft laws including "On Territorial Defense" and "On Migration." Amendments to laws on privatization, state financial control, and the Tax Code were also reviewed. The Council considered a draft law amending the Housing Code and discussed a credit agreement for road reconstruction, along with a protocol on refugee assistance.

item.title: Authorities Deny Danger Amid Hospital Lockdowns Following Researcher's Death
item.description: Following the death of a researcher at an Irkutsk plague institute, over 60 employees were reportedly isolated. While media speculated about plague or lab accidents, Rospotrebnadzor denied these claims, attributing the death to pneumonia. However, patients reported hospital lockdowns, with family visits restricted and no one allowed to leave. A mask mandate was also implemented at a local aluminum plant.

item.title: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Meets with UNESCO Representative to Discuss Water and Cryosphere Initiatives
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Mukhriddin met with UNESCO's acting Assistant Director-General for Natural Sciences, Abu Amani. They discussed the implementation of the Decade of Action for the Cryosphere (2025–2034) and preparations for the 2028 UN Water Conference in Dushanbe. Cooperation in water resources, glacier studies, and science was also reviewed.
